title: Orcid Integration
definition: The integration of ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID) into a system to enable verification of user identities and enhance trust in knowledge contributions.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a digital system that checks if you're the real person you claim to be. ORCID integration makes this possible, allowing the system to confirm your identity and give you a green badge, which shows that you're the legitimate owner of your ORCID.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: ORCID integration involves fetching public ORCID profiles and creating verification provenance blocks. This enhances the trust in knowledge contributions by providing a means to verify user identities, although it's important to note that the badge indicates 'claimed' verification rather than 'owner-verified'.
difficulty_levels.expert: ORCID integration is a form of third-party authentication that allows the system to trust the ownership and control of a digital identity. It enhances the credibility of knowledge contributions, but it's essential to understand that public API version can't prove ownership, as full verification requires OAuth. This is a limitation that needs to be documented and understood by the users.

extra_fields.insight: The integration of ORCID into a system provides a means to verify user identities and enhance trust in knowledge contributions, although it's important to understand the limitations of the public API version.
